summary: This note is an overview of electricity as a set of physical phenomena tied to electric charge and its motion, linked to magnetism through electromagnetism. It covers the history from ancient observations of electric fish and static electricity through Franklin, Faraday, Maxwell, and the transistor, then explains core concepts: charge, current, electric fields, potential, electromagnets, circuits, power, and electronics. The text is truncated mid-section on electromagnetic waves.
one_line: Overview of electricity: its history from ancient static and electric fish to modern electronics, and its core physical concepts of charge, current, fields, and circuits.
key_facts: Electricity is the set of physical phenomena associated with the presence and motion of matter possessing an electric charge.
Thales of Miletus made observations on static electricity around 600 BCE.
William Gilbert wrote De Magnete in 1600 and coined the Neo-Latin word electricus from the Greek elektron meaning amber.
Benjamin Franklin's kite experiment in June 1752 showed that lightning was electrical in nature.
Alessandro Volta's voltaic pile of 1800 was made from alternating layers of zinc and copper.
Michael Faraday invented the electric motor in 1821.
Georg Ohm mathematically analysed the electrical circuit in 1827.
James Clerk Maxwell linked electricity, magnetism and light in 'On Physical Lines of Force' in 1861 and 1862.
The first working transistor, a germanium-based point-contact transistor, was invented by John Bardeen and Walter Houser Brattain at Bell Labs in 1947.
Coulomb's law determines the force between electric charges and has an inverse-square relation to the distance between them.
By convention, the charge carried by electrons is deemed negative, a custom that originated with the work of Benjamin Franklin.
Air tends to arc across small gaps at electric field strengths exceeding 30 kV per centimetre.
The voltage of a large lightning cloud may be as high as 100 MV and have discharge energies as great as 250 kWh.
The ohm is the resistance that produces a potential difference of one volt in response to a current of one amp.
Electric power P equals IV, where I is current in amperes and V is voltage in volts.

entities.name: Thales of Miletus
entities.role: made a series of observations on static electricity around 600 BCE and wrongly believed the attraction was magnetic

entities.name: Benjamin Franklin
entities.role: conducted extensive 18th-century research on electricity and flew a kite in a storm in June 1752

entities.name: William Gilbert
entities.role: English scientist who wrote De Magnete in 1600 and coined the word electricus

entities.name: Joseph Priestley
entities.role: author of History and Present Status of Electricity (1767), with whom Franklin corresponded

entities.name: Michael Faraday
entities.role: invented the electric motor in 1821, invented the first electrical generator in 1831, and introduced the concept of the electric field

entities.name: Hans Christian Ørsted
entities.role: discovered in 1820 that a current-carrying wire disturbs a magnetic compass needle, establishing electromagnetism

entities.name: André-Marie Ampère
entities.role: investigated electromagnetism and showed parallel current-carrying wires attract or repel depending on current direction

entities.name: Georg Ohm
entities.role: mathematically analysed the electrical circuit in 1827; the ohm unit is named after him

entities.name: James Clerk Maxwell
entities.role: linked electricity, magnetism and light, and analysed electromagnetic waves theoretically in 1864

entities.name: Alessandro Volta
entities.role: created the voltaic pile battery of 1800

entities.name: Luigi Galvani
entities.role: published in 1791 his discovery of bioelectromagnetics

entities.name: Albert Einstein
entities.role: explained the photoelectric effect in 1905 and received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for it

entities.name: Heinrich Hertz
entities.role: discovered in 1887 that electrodes illuminated with ultraviolet light create sparks more easily

entities.name: John Bardeen
entities.role: co-inventor of the first working transistor at Bell Labs in 1947

entities.name: Walter Houser Brattain
entities.role: co-inventor of the first working transistor at Bell Labs in 1947

entities.name: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb
entities.role: investigated charge in the late eighteenth century and deduced that charge manifests in two opposing forms

entities.name: Michael Faraday
entities.role: also gave the farad unit of capacitance its name

entities.name: Bell Labs
entities.role: institution where the first working transistor was invented in 1947

entities.name: Joseph Henry
entities.role: contemporary of Faraday after whom the henry unit of inductance is named

entities.name: Nicholson and Carlisle
entities.role: discovered in 1800 that water could be decomposed by current from a voltaic pile

entities.name: Lightning conductor
entities.role: device whose sharp spike encourages lightning to strike it rather than the building it protects

entities.name: Baghdad Battery
entities.role: artifact discovered in 1936 that resembles a galvanic cell, possibly linked to Parthian electroplating
